apps/server/src/serverSettings.ts.why: Every settings write goes through upstream's patch and write paths here. The lines from "import { renameRetiredAutoUpdateKeys }" on predate this list and record main as it was when every upstream file began to count (#277); they are to move into apps/server/src/fork/ (follow-up), and the file cannot grow meanwhile.

apps/server/src/peer/RemoteDelegation.ts.why: #386: a remote delegate_task interrupted after its launch there (the parent's turn moved on) still records and follows its task: the launch, record and follow run as one uninterruptible step. A launch recorded with no task here is stopped there with a warning, as a failed record is. Tested in apps/server/src/fork/remoteDelegationAbortSafe.test.ts. Upstream PR pingdotgg/t3code#30249 (record before launch) rewrites this block, and its intent differs: after an interrupted, uncertain launch it stops the child there, while this seam keeps the child and follows it. Whoever brings #30249 in through fork-follow must choose on purpose between stopping and keeping (and expect a merge conflict on this block), then drop this seam or keep it.

//pending: Upstream files whose fork lines predate counting every upstream file, each with its ceiling: the most fork lines it may hold against upstream (counted from upstream, as fork-follow runs the check). To move into fork files or pin as seams; lower a ceiling when lines move out and take a file off when none are left. A pull request may change them but not grow them.
//forkFiles: Files upstream does not have that are not named as fork files (a fork, fork-*, forkName or FORK_* folder or file). A pull request's run, which has no upstream commit, takes them for the fork's own. dir/ is everything under it, ** any folders, * any characters but /, !path never. A pattern that matches an upstream file fails the check from upstream.
//lost: Seam and pending files that lost upstream lines, counted from upstream (as fork-follow runs the check): "lines", the upstream lines not kept in order and indentation; "gone", those whose text is gone. Held exactly, like a ceiling; an unlisted file counts 0. Lower a count when a line comes back, and keep each one small: a count is not a set of lines, so a line counted here may move unseen, and in a pending file a pull request can put back one gone upstream line and delete another with both counts unchanged.
